subject: route-plan mode chattering near dependency-completeness safety threshold
hypothesis: A fail-closed asymmetric hysteresis policy can reduce TARGETED_DELTA/DENSE_FANOUT mode thrashing without permitting targeted routing below the declared completeness safety threshold.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Hysteresis merely hides instability by spending substantially more dense-fanout cost, so it is not Pareto-superior and may be unnecessary if route-plan recomputation is cheap.

method.completeness_trace: bounded deterministic multi-frequency oscillation around 0.90 with fixed-seed noise plus one degradation burst and one recovery burst
method.hysteresis_policy: fail closed TARGETED->DENSE immediately below 0.90; DENSE->TARGETED only at completeness >= 0.95
method.rollback: remove this control candidate; retain v3 route-plan rules unchanged

interpretation: Asymmetric hysteresis materially reduces route-mode chattering in this canary while preserving fail-closed completeness, but the modeled network-cost penalty is large. Route-mode switch rate and re-entry hysteresis width should therefore be measured in real-repo v2/v3 replay rather than silently hard-coded.
architecture_delta: NO_PROMOTION; add route_mode_switch_rate, dwell_time and hysteresis-width sweep to the existing live-fusion real-replay/fault matrix if execution cost permits.
controls: route stability does not mint evidence or effect authority
no architecture promotion from synthetic evidence
